quickAnswer: Lunenburg runs on delivered fuel: 57.8% of occupied homes heat with oil, 9.7% with bottled gas and only 17.3% with utility gas (ACS 2022). A replacement here often starts with oil versus a heat pump, and Mass HVAC assesses the home's heating load before quoting a system.
body: ## Oil, bottled gas and wood in a town with little pipeline gas

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), Lunenburg has 4,738 housing units, and the heating numbers are the first thing to know. Fuel oil or kerosene heats 2,652 occupied homes, or 57.8%, the 12th-highest share among the 50 towns we serve and far above the 36.5% of the middle town. Bottled or tank (LP) gas heats another 445 homes (9.7%), 7th-highest of the 50. Wood is the heating fuel in 378 homes (8.2%).

Utility gas reaches only 792 homes (17.3%), which ranks 43rd of 50. When a boiler or furnace fails, the choices often include a new oil or LP system or a heat pump. A switch to natural gas depends on a main being available at the street, and only the gas company can confirm that. Oil and LP both arrive by delivery, so the tank and the supply arrangement are part of any replacement decision. We also assess the home's heating load before quoting, because a new unit sized from the old nameplate can be too big.
## An older core with a young edge

The median Lunenburg home was built in 1971, against 1975 for the middle town. The town also has the 4th-highest share of homes built since 2010 among the 50: 686 homes (14.5%) date from 2010 or later, and 1,152 (24.3%) from 2000 or later. At the other end, 841 homes (17.8%) were built in 1939 or earlier, and 2,853 (60.2%) before 1980.

That spread means two different jobs. Older houses often leak more air, and an old distribution system may not suit a newer, differently sized unit. Newer houses are generally tighter, which helps with comfort and puts more weight on ventilation and correct sizing. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $393,200, versus $579,150 for the middle town, so the cost of a system is worth weighing against what the house is worth, and a partial fix is sometimes the sensible plan.
## Unitil, the highways and the town's early history

Lunenburg's electric utility is Unitil, an investor-owned company. Mass Save heat pump rebates depend on the rules for the utility that serves the address, so confirm at masssave.com before you buy equipment. The [heat pump page](/cities/lunenburg/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) lays out the 2026 whole-home rebate terms and the weatherization condition.

The town covers 27.7 square miles, of which 26.4 are land. Three state highways run through it: Route 2A along Mass Ave, Route 13 along Electric Ave and Chase Road, and Route 225, which starts in Lunenburg and follows West Groton Road.

Lunenburg was first settled by Europeans in 1718 and incorporated in 1728, and parts of neighboring Fitchburg were once Lunenburg, breaking away around 1764. Houses from 2000 onward share the town with 841 that predate 1940.

Whalom Park, on Whalom Lake, was a noted amusement park through much of the 20th century and closed in 2000, and the public library began in 1853. Lunenburg is bordered by Townsend, Shirley, Lancaster, Leominster, Fitchburg and Ashby.

Renters live in 879 households, 19.2% of the town. In a rental, the landlord pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise, so a heating failure is a legal matter as well as a comfort problem. The maintenance page covers the seasonal checks.

faq.q: Is it worth converting an oil system to natural gas in Lunenburg?
faq.a: Only if a gas main runs past your house, and only the gas company can confirm that. With only 17.3% of Lunenburg homes on utility gas, a main may not pass every house. A free written estimate can set a like-for-like oil replacement, a conversion where available and a heat pump side by side.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to replace a furnace or boiler in Lunenburg?
faq.a: Usually yes for gas equipment. Only licensed plumbers and gas fitters may pull gas permits in Massachusetts, and a new gas furnace or boiler normally needs a permit and a final inspection. Check with the town's building department. Oil and LP work can have separate rules.

faq.q: Our house was built after 2010. Does it still need a heating load assessment?
faq.a: Yes. A newer house is usually tighter, but its heating and cooling load still depends on its size, windows and layout. We assess the load before quoting a system, whatever the build year, so the equipment is neither oversized nor undersized.

faq.q: Who is Lunenburg's electric utility, and does it affect heat pump rebates?
faq.a: The electric utility is Unitil. Rebate eligibility depends on the program rules for the utility that serves your address, so confirm at masssave.com before you install anything. The 2026 whole-home terms are laid out on the heat pump page, and eligibility for a given address cannot be promised.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Only 792 Lunenburg homes use utility gas (ACS 2022), so replacements often involve oil, LP, wood or electric systems. A written estimate and a heating-load assessment come before any quote.
body: ## Replacing heat when gas is the exception

Utility gas heats 792 occupied homes in Lunenburg, 43rd of 50 among the towns we serve, so a gas furnace permit applies to a smaller group of homes. For the many homes on oil, a replacement often raises the question of a new oil boiler or furnace versus a heat pump that carries part of the load. The median home dates to 1971, and old equipment tends to be less efficient and costlier to keep repairing.
### What matters first

- The fuel and tank in place now, and whether the tank is still in good shape.
- Where the distribution runs: baseboard, radiators or ducts can decide whether a swap is simple.
- Chimney or venting condition, since a new, more efficient unit can vent differently from the old one.
- Whether a heat pump with the old system kept as backup suits the house.
### Wood in the mix

The Census lists 378 Lunenburg homes as heated mainly with wood. Where wood is the main heat, a second source can matter on days when nobody is home to feed the fire. The median Lunenburg home dates to 1971, and 2,853 homes (60.2%) predate 1980, ranking 20th of 50 for that share. Houses in that group may have a boiler and piping of similar vintage, so look at the whole system when one part fails.
### Rentals and the heat rules

Renters hold 879 of the 4,589 occupied homes (19.2%), ranking 21st of 50. Under 105 CMR 410.201, a rented unit must stay at 68 F or warmer during waking hours and at 64 F or warmer overnight through the heating season, and the landlord pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise. That is general information, not legal advice. A dead boiler in a rented house is urgent.
### Gas permits when they apply

For the 792 homes with a gas connection, the permit has to come from a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and a new furnace or boiler normally ends with an inspection. The town's building department can explain local steps.
### Emergency repairs
If the heat quits, call (508) 786-8755. The line takes emergency calls around the clock. For cooling or heat pump work, see the [heat pump page](/cities/lunenburg/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is a new oil boiler the only choice for a Lunenburg house on oil?
faq.a: No. Another oil unit is one path and can make sense when the tank and the pipes are sound. A heat pump that takes most of the load, with a boiler left in place for severe nights, is another. The tank, the distribution and the house settle it.

faq.q: When does a heating repair stop making sense?
faq.a: A single failed part on a fairly new boiler or furnace is normally worth fixing. A cracked heat exchanger, or repair bills that grow each winter, usually argue for a new unit.

faq.q: Does it matter that so few Lunenburg homes use utility gas?
faq.a: It narrows the choices. Utility gas heats 17.3% of occupied homes here, against 41.9% in the middle town of the 50, so most replacements are oil, LP, wood, electric or a heat pump. A gas switch depends on a main at the street, which only the gas company can confirm.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses make up 74.4% of Lunenburg's housing (ACS 2022), 18.8% of units sit in multi-unit buildings and 175 are mobile homes. Ducted, ductless and heat pump cooling each suit different buildings.
body: ## Cooling a mix of houses, apartments and mobile homes

The ACS counts 3,527 single-family detached homes in Lunenburg (74.4% of housing units), 143 attached townhouses (3.0%), 175 mobile homes (3.7%) and 893 homes in multi-unit buildings (18.8%). Buildings of 5 or more units hold 454 of them. Each type has its own cooling puzzle.
### Detached houses

Central cooling needs ducts with room for the airflow, so in a detached house the first check is which duct runs already exist. Older houses, such as the 841 built in 1939 or earlier, may have little space for them. Where ducts are missing, a ductless mini-split puts a small indoor head in each room or zone and needs only a thin line set to the outdoor unit.
### Mobile homes and small apartments

Mobile homes often have limited wall and roof space and their own electrical limits, so the equipment and the mounting have to suit the structure. In apartments, a ductless head can cool one unit without touching the rest of the building. Electrical capacity is part of the question in both.
### Newer houses

Homes from 2000 on, 1,152 units (24.3%), tend to be tighter than the older stock. A tighter house can hold cool air well but can also hold humidity, which makes correct sizing matter more, since an oversized unit cools quickly and shuts off before it dries the air.
### The newest homes

Lunenburg ranks 4th of 50 for housing built since 2010: 686 units, or 14.5%, against 8.4% for the middle town. For these newest homes, a cooling plan starts from whatever duct layout and electrical capacity the house already has, and the tighter shell makes humidity control worth asking about. A system that is sized to the real load, and not to the largest room, keeps the air drier and cycles less often.
### Electric homes
Only 308 homes (6.7%) heat with electricity here, 44th of 50. In an electrically heated home, one heat pump can cool in summer and heat in winter, and the sizing has to be worked out for both.
### Repair or replace
A weak cooling unit is not always a dead one. A failed capacitor, low refrigerant from a leak or a dirty coil can be repaired. A failed compressor in an old system often points to replacement.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a Lunenburg house with baseboard heat and no ducts?
faq.a: Yes. A mini-split needs no ducts, only a slim line set between each indoor head and the outdoor unit. We size it from the rooms to be cooled and choose where the outdoor unit can sit.
For a single bedroom it may do. Across several rooms, mini-split heads tend to run quieter and leave the windows clear, though the house has the final say.

faq.q: Can a mobile home use a mini-split?
faq.a: Often, yes, if the electrical supply and the wall or mounting suit the equipment.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Lunenburg's electric utility is Unitil, an investor-owned company. With 57.8% of homes on oil and 9.7% on LP gas, a heat pump is a live option for many households, and the rebate terms are on our overview page.
body: ## Heat pumps in an oil and LP town

Oil heats 2,652 Lunenburg homes and LP gas heats 445, so a large part of the town buys fuel by delivery. A heat pump moves some or all of that load onto electricity, and a cold-climate model heats in winter and cools in summer. Electricity is the main heat in only 308 homes (6.7%), 44th of 50, so most households would be adding a new kind of system.
### Unitil and the rebate

Unitil is investor-owned rather than municipal. Under Mass Save's 2026 rules the whole-home rebate pays $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500 per home, after the house has been weatherized. Details live on our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits). Eligibility cannot be promised for an address, so confirm with Mass Save before signing a contract.
### The age test against Lunenburg's housing

The weatherization step has a shortcut for homes built in 2000 or later. In Lunenburg that is 1,152 units (24.3%), including 686 built in 2010 or later. That leaves 841 homes from 1939 or earlier and 1,145 from 1940 to 1959, plus the 867 and 733 in the two bands between 1960 and 1999. For all of them, a Home Energy Assessment is the other route to passing the test. Lunenburg is 46th of 50 for median home value ($393,200), which is worth keeping in mind when weighing a project's cost against the house.
### Ducts, baseboard and mobile homes

Where radiators or baseboard carry the heat, ductless heads avoid new duct runs. Where sound ducts already exist, a ducted heat pump can use them. The ACS counts 3,527 detached houses, 893 units in multi-unit buildings and 175 mobile homes, and each asks a different question about wall space, electrical capacity and mounting.
### Wood and the old boiler

Wood is the main heat in 378 homes (8.2%). A heat pump can run beside a stove as the everyday source. In an oil house, the old boiler can stay for the coldest nights if the heating load calls for it. We assess that load before quoting, and the [heating page](/cities/lunenburg/heating-installation-repair) covers the replacement side of the same choice.

faq.q: Does being on Unitil change what I can claim?
faq.a: Possibly. Rebate rules can depend on the utility serving an address, and Lunenburg's utility is Unitil. Check your address with Mass Save before you sign, because we cannot promise eligibility.

faq.q: Is a 1971 house too old for a heat pump?
faq.a: Age alone does not rule it out. The median Lunenburg home dates to 1971 (ACS 2022). The heating load, the insulation and the weatherization step matter more than the year.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace an oil tank entirely?
faq.a: In some houses it can carry most of the load, and in others it shares the work with another source. A heating-load assessment settles it, not a rule of thumb.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil heats more than half of Lunenburg homes, and LP and wood heat hundreds more. Oil burners need a yearly cleaning, and a tune-up can catch problems before a January breakdown.
body: ## Tune-ups for a town that burns delivered fuel

Maintenance in Lunenburg is mostly about combustion. For the 2,652 oil homes, the yearly visit means cleaning the burner, swapping the nozzle and filter and testing combustion. LP equipment needs its burner, venting and controls checked. Wood stoves and chimneys often need cleaning too, and a qualified chimney sweep is the right person for that part.
### Gas homes are the minority

The 792 homes on utility gas still need a yearly safety and efficiency check of the burner, venting and controls, but they are the smaller group. Heat pumps need clean filters and coils and a check of refrigerant-side performance each year.
### Rentals

Owners hold 3,710 of the town's 4,589 occupied homes (80.8%), so for most households the service schedule is a personal choice. The 879 rented homes (19.2%) are usually serviced at the landlord's call, and a pre-winter visit costs less than an emergency in January.
### Other fuels

The Census lists 14 homes under other fuel or coal. Equipment that burns an unusual fuel can still benefit from a yearly look at controls and venting. Lunenburg's median build year is 1971, and the Census puts 2,853 homes (60.2%) before 1980. A house of that age may carry a boiler or furnace that has run many seasons, so the yearly visit doubles as a check on condition. Rank matters here as well: Lunenburg is 20th of 50 for homes built before 1980 and 12th for oil heat, which puts older houses and oil burners together in a good share of the town. A technician who knows the boiler's history can compare this year's readings with last year's and flag a slow decline before it becomes a breakdown. The 1,152 homes from 2000 or later usually have newer equipment, though filters, drains and outdoor units need attention there too.
### Seasonal rhythm

- **Late summer to early fall:** oil, LP and gas heating tune-ups, before the first cold nights.
- **Spring:** cooling and heat pump checks, before the first warm stretch.
- **Any time:** noise, odor, short cycling or soot is a reason to call early.
### Newer systems still need care
Newer systems still need filter changes, clear condensate drains and clean outdoor units, whatever the age of the house.
### Before you call
It helps to have the fuel, the approximate age of the unit, the nameplate details if readable and what you noticed.

faq.q: How often should an oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Yearly, ahead of the first cold nights, is the usual interval. A missed cleaning can leave soot on the heat exchanger and wear on the burner.

faq.q: Should a landlord service the boiler before winter?
faq.a: Yes, it is good practice. When one boiler heats several households, a failure reaches all of them, so a visit before the season is cheap insurance.

faq.q: What gets checked on an LP system?
faq.a: LP gas heats 445 Lunenburg homes (9.7%), 7th highest of the 50 towns. We check the burner, the venting and the controls, and look over the connection to the tank.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Lunenburg's housing runs from 1939-and-earlier houses to ones built after 2010, and 378 homes burn wood. A wood stove, a damp basement or a tight house can each call for a different fix.
body: ## Air quality across the town's age bands

The Census sorts Lunenburg's housing into age bands, from 841 homes built in 1939 or earlier up to 686 built since 2010. A mixed town means no single recommendation fits every house, and the right first step is a look at the building in question.
### Houses from the 1940 to 1959 band

The 1940 to 1959 band has 1,145 homes (24.2%). Houses of that age can have older ductwork, if they have any, and older insulation. Anyone opening walls in an older house should have a qualified specialist test for older materials first. Dust, pollen and damp air can get in through gaps.
### Tighter newer houses

Homes built since 2000 are generally tighter. A tight shell saves energy, but it also holds in moisture and cooking fumes. Ventilation is the counterweight: a bath fan ducted outdoors and a range hood both do real work.
### Wood smoke

With 378 homes heating with wood, stove operation and chimney condition matter. Keep the chimney and flue clean, burn dry wood and make sure there is a working carbon monoxide alarm. Any fuel-burning appliance should have one nearby. Oil heats 2,652 homes here and LP gas 445, so many households have a burner inside the building, and each needs clear venting and a chimney in good condition. A yearly service is the way to catch a problem before it reaches the living space.
### Humidity
Winter heating dries indoor air, and humid summers can reverse that. Older basements are often damp, and a dehumidifier eases the air while the water source needs its own fix.
### What we can do

- Upgrade filtration and keep filters changed on schedule.
- Add a humidifier or dehumidifier tied to the system.
- Fix or add ventilation for tight homes.
- Clean ducts that are visibly dirty or damaged, and find the cause so they do not fill again.

Mobile homes, 175 in the Census count, and the 893 units in multi-unit buildings are homes where, as a general matter, cooking moisture and odors can spread through a small or shared space, so fans and filter care matter there too. Ask us to look at ventilation first, since it costs less than most equipment changes. For heating equipment checks, see the [maintenance page](/cities/lunenburg/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Only if they show dirt, mold or damage. We inspect the system first and say plainly whether a cleaning would help.

faq.q: Is a newer house automatically healthier to breathe in?
faq.a: Not automatically. Newer houses are usually tighter, so ventilation matters more. A bath fan, a range hood and regular filter changes help in houses of any age.

faq.q: Do newer Lunenburg homes need ventilation work?
faq.a: They can. Tighter construction is typical of recent decades, and Lunenburg ranks 4th of 50 for homes built since 2010. A tight house relies on its fans and filters to move air, so those are worth checking, along with the filter size and the last time it was changed.
